resolutions.researcher_notes: No source states 'operating' verbatim for this specific line, but two independent sources support an in-service status: MEED reports the Hawiyah-to-Uthmaniyah pipeline package reached mechanical completion (April 2007), and Aramco's Master Gas System article describes Uthmaniyah/Hawiyah as active nodes of the operating national gas network. The Haradh/Hawiyah increment feeding this line is in production. Status 'operating' is well-supported by implication; medium because no source uses an explicit current-status word for this segment.

Fuel=Gas corroborated by two independent origins. AramcoExpats (archived Aramco content) describes the increment gas piped through a 56-inch 'rich gas pipeline' from Hawiyah to Uthmaniyah for deep ethane recovery; MEED describes the Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah line as part of the sales-gas/NGL Hawiyah gas program. Both confirm a natural-gas service.

No source states 56 km for this specific line; the figure appears GEM route-derived. Available published lengths for adjacent/parallel Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah lines differ: MEED gives a 57 km 24-inch NGL line (Hawiyah NGL plant to Uthmaniyah); Aramco material cites a 160 km 56-inch sales-gas line (Hawiyah to Booster Gas Compression Station-1) and a 1 km 56-inch section tying into the Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah gas line (HUG-1). 56 km is plausible as the straight Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah corridor distance but is unsourced; flag for possible conflation with the 57 km NGL line. UNRESOLVED.

Diameter 56 in supported by AramcoExpats (archived Aramco content): the increment gas is 'piped through a new 56\" rich gas pipeline to Uthmaniyah for deep ethane recovery.' Single origin (Aramco), so medium. CONTRADICTION to flag: MEED describes a parallel Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah line as 24-inch (57 km NGL line) and a 28-inch Uthmaniyah-Shedgum line -- these are different, co-located pipelines, not this row. The 56-inch value is correct for the rich/sales-gas line this row represents, but the multiple co-located Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah lines (24, 28, 56 inch) are a duplication/segmentation risk worth checking.

Both endpoints in Saudi Arabia corroborated by two independent origins: the Hawiyah and Uthmaniyah gas plants are both in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. AramcoExpats and MEED both place the Hawiyah-Uthmaniyah pipeline in Saudi Arabia.

Owner Saudi Aramco (100%) corroborated by two independent origins. The Hawiyah/Uthmaniyah gas plants and the increment pipelines are Saudi Aramco assets (AramcoExpats/Aramco content); MEED attributes the Hawiyah pipeline program to Saudi Aramco. No other equity holder mentioned; 100% Aramco is consistent with all sources.
